Find the $x$-coordinate of the point on the curve $y=\sqrt{5x+4}$ that is closest to the point $(2,0).$ Do not round the answer.

$x=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Let us consider the *squared* distance $S$ between $(2,0)$ and a general point $P(x,y)$:

$$
S=(x-2)^{2}+{y}^{2}
$$

We require that the point $P$ lies on the curve $y=\sqrt{5x+4}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}S(x) & =(x-2)^{2}+{y}^{2} \\  & =(x-2)^{2}+(\sqrt{5x+4})^{2} \\  & =(x-2)^{2}+5x+4 \\  & ={x}^{2}-4x+4+5x+4 \\  & ={x}^{2}+x+8.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the minimum distance, we take the first derivative of $S(x)$ and equate it to zero. This gives the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}^{′}(x)=2x+1 & =0 \\ 2x & =-1 \\ x & =-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

We can see that ${S}^{″}(x)=2>0.$ Therefore, $x=-\frac{1}{2}$ is a minimum of $S.$

So, the squared distance (and therefore the actual distance) is minimized when $x=-\frac{1}{2}.$
